overall_summary: Bitcoin is steady near sixty-four thousand after heavy weekend liquidations, with some institutional dip-buying providing support. A stronger dollar, sticky yields, and fresh geopolitical flashpoints from the Middle East to Ukraine keep the broader tone cautious. Today's US data will likely set the next short-term direction.
key_points: Institutions buy the dip; Grayscale constructive
DXY and yields pressure risk assets
Key US data due amid mixed backdrop

items.title: Wintermute Warns BTC Could Slide to $50Ks
items.summary: Market maker Wintermute says Bitcoin's bear phase is far from over after it lost the 200-week moving average near sixty-eight thousand. They cite ninety-two percent odds of a December Fed hike, ten-year yields back above five percent, shrinking stablecoin supply, and weak ETF plus treasury demand. Traders should care because a major liquidity provider sees the path of least resistance still lower, with sixty-two thousand then the dense sixty thousand put wall as next magnets.
items.impact: Heightens downside risk and defensive positioning ahead of Fed and Nvidia events

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs End Seven-Day Outflow Streak
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs took in a net seven point nine million dollars on Monday, snapping a seven-session outflow run that had drained roughly one point nine billion. BlackRock's IBIT led with seventy-six point five million in, ending its own eleven-day streak, though Grayscale GBTC and others offset most of the gains. Traders should watch this closely as even a tiny reversal after heavy redemptions can signal whether institutional selling pressure is finally easing.
items.impact: Removes immediate flow headwind but remains too small to reverse broader November outflows

items.title: BTC Holds Near $64K After $2B Weekend Liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin slid to about sixty-two thousand over the weekend, its lowest since July, as roughly two billion dollars in leveraged positions were wiped out, mostly longs. It has stabilized near sixty-four thousand with extreme fear readings, while Nasdaq slid further ahead of Nvidia's first earnings without Jensen Huang. Traders care because the flush cleaned speculative leverage, yet the bounce has stalled below the two-hundred-week average with retail sales and Fed minutes still ahead.
items.impact: Leverage reset offers healthier base but unresolved support leaves event risk elevated

items.title: Tether-Backed Twenty One Capital Buys $10M BTC Dip
items.summary: Twenty One Capital, the Tether-backed public Bitcoin treasury firm, purchased one hundred fifty-four Bitcoin for about ten million dollars in cash at an average of roughly sixty-four thousand eight hundred. It was their first reported buy since listing and lifts holdings to about forty-three thousand six hundred sixty-eight BTC; Strategy separately added four hundred eighty-five BTC last week. Traders should note these corporate buys against the grain as a sign some large holders still see value after the selloff.
items.impact: Supports narrative of opportunistic treasury accumulation amid weakness

items.title: Grayscale Calls $64K Pullback Compelling Entry Point
items.summary: Grayscale's head of research said the recent crypto slide, with Bitcoin near sixty-four thousand after a roughly seventeen percent November drop, offers compelling entry points for medium- to long-term investors. He pointed to solid fundamentals, oversold conditions after stablecoin outflows and AI stock spillover, plus ongoing deficit spending supporting alternative stores of value. This counters the Wintermute caution and gives bulls a high-profile institutional voice arguing the damage creates opportunity rather than more pain.
items.impact: Provides counter-narrative that could encourage dip-buying by longer-horizon capital

items.title: Optimizely Hack Hits Ledger and 177 Sites with Crypto Clipper
items.summary: Attackers injected malware via the Optimizely web-testing platform into scripts on one hundred seventy-eight major sites including Ledger, HSBC, BBC and Zoom. The code swapped crypto wallet addresses on pages and clipboards for the attacker's and skimmed cards; only a few thousand dollars appear stolen before wallets were emptied and the code removed. Traders should care because it underscores ongoing supply-chain and browser risks for crypto users even when hardware wallets are involved, though direct market impact stayed minimal.
items.impact: Heightens security caution with limited immediate price effect

items.title: DXY Hits 19-Month High Near 103.70 on Hike Bets
items.summary: The US dollar index climbed to a fresh 19-month peak around 103.70 before easing slightly, driven by firm Fed rate-hike expectations after recent hot inflation readings. Markets now price a high probability of a December quarter-point increase, with some chance of 50 basis points. Crypto traders should watch this closely because a stronger dollar and tighter financial conditions typically pressure Bitcoin and risk assets by raising opportunity costs and liquidity headwinds.
items.impact: Stronger USD and higher rate odds weigh on crypto and equities

items.title: Empire State Factory Index Slumps to 7.8
items.summary: New York Fed's Empire State Manufacturing Survey dropped sharply to 7.8 in November from 25.5 in October, well below expectations near 17-18. New orders cooled significantly while employment hit a multi-year high and prices moderated somewhat. This mixed regional signal comes ahead of national retail sales and industrial production, offering an early read on whether growth is cooling enough to temper Fed hawkishness—key for risk assets if it fuels growth-scare narratives.
items.impact: Soft activity data could ease rate fears but signals potential slowdown

items.title: Fed Chair Warsh Flags AI Risks and Opportunities
items.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh spoke on Monday about artificial intelligence, calling it super intelligence that could supercharge productivity and growth or cause job disruption and inequality. He said Fed staff are sketching contingencies and the technology will have significant monetary-policy implications down the road, without giving direct rate guidance. Traders care because any signal on how AI affects inflation, employment or the neutral rate can shift expectations for the path of policy and risk appetite.
items.impact: Long-term productivity hopes vs near-term policy uncertainty

items.title: Treasury Yields Hold Elevated Near 5.12% Ahead of Data
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield hovered around 5.12 to 5.13 percent on Monday and into Tuesday, easing only modestly after last week's jump on inflation and hawkish Fed talk. Two-year yields also stayed firm while markets fully price a December hike. Elevated yields raise discount rates for growth assets and crypto, so any soft retail sales print today could pull them lower and give Bitcoin breathing room, while a hot number would reinforce the hawkish backdrop.
items.impact: High yields continue to pressure risk assets and liquidity

items.title: China October Data Misses: Retail and Output Weaken
items.summary: China's retail sales rose just 0.4 percent year-over-year in October, missing forecasts, while industrial production slowed to 4.8 percent and fixed-asset investment contracted further. The soft domestic demand readings highlight ongoing property and consumer weakness despite export strength. For global markets and crypto this matters as China growth affects commodity prices, risk sentiment and dollar strength—another soft print reinforces concerns about the world's second-largest economy.
items.impact: Weaker China growth weighs on global risk appetite and commodities

items.title: Retail Sales and Industrial Production Due Today
items.summary: US advance retail sales for October and industrial production plus capacity utilization are scheduled for release this morning Eastern time, with retail sales expected to slow to around 0.2 percent month-over-month from 0.8 percent. FOMC minutes follow tomorrow and several Fed speakers are on tap. These are the key near-term catalysts that can confirm or challenge the hawkish pivot priced into markets—crypto traders need to watch for beats that firm the dollar and yields or misses that ease pressure.
items.impact: Data will drive near-term rate expectations and dollar moves

items.title: Trump, Xi, Putin Hold Historic Trilateral Summit in Shenzhen
items.summary: President Trump is in Asia for Quad and ASEAN talks before a groundbreaking three-way meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on Thursday. The agenda covers nuclear arms control, the Iran war, Ukraine, trade and economics, with China calling it groundbreaking for world peace. Traders should watch closely because any signal of de-escalation or new great-power deals could ease geopolitical risk premiums across risk assets including Bitcoin.
items.impact: Potential volatility spike around summit outcomes on peace and trade

items.title: Ukraine Collapses Section of Kerch Bridge in Major Strike
items.summary: Ukraine hit the strategic Kerch Bridge to occupied Crimea with drones and missiles in what Zelensky called an unprecedented multi-week operation, collapsing a road arch span into the water and damaging the rail section. Russia reported intercepting a record number of drones overnight while striking bridges in Kyiv. This escalates the war logistically and symbolically just before Trump-Putin talks, raising uncertainty that often pressures risk assets.
items.impact: Heightened war risk premium and possible oil/energy volatility

items.title: Third US Carrier Arrives as Iran Tensions and Hormuz Attacks Persist
items.summary: The USS Theodore Roosevelt has joined two other carriers in the Middle East, giving Trump more options while a naval blockade of Iran continues and tankers keep hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Vice President Vance insists there will be no forever war even as Iran targets Bahrain and diplomacy stalls. Energy shipping risks remain elevated, which can quickly feed into oil prices and broader risk-off moves for crypto.
items.impact: Elevated oil and shipping risk that weighs on risk appetite

items.title: US Intel Warns of Iranian Dirty Bomb Plot Targeting DC Officials
items.summary: US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans for a dirty bomb or chemical attack in Washington aimed at senior Trump administration officials, with specific locations noted though no imminent threat is confirmed. The White House says there are currently no credible homeland threats, and Iran rejects the chemical weapons claims. This kind of black-swan headline can spark sudden risk-off flows even if officials downplay it.
items.impact: Fear-driven risk-off pressure and higher volatility

items.title: Russia Aircraft Violate Japanese Airspace; Jets Scrambled
items.summary: Japan scrambled fighters and protested after two suspected Russian military aircraft entered its airspace near Okinoshima for several minutes early Tuesday. South Korea and Taiwan also responded to Russian planes in their air defense zones as the aircraft headed toward the Pacific. The timing ahead of the Trump-Xi-Putin summit raises Asia tension just as major leaders gather, adding another layer of geopolitical noise for markets.
items.impact: Regional tension that could amplify summit-related uncertainty

items.title: Houthis Regain Control Near Bab al-Mandab Shipping Chokepoint
items.summary: Iran-backed Houthis have taken back positions overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait after Saudi-backed Yemeni forces redeployed to defend Aden. The waterway handles a significant share of global trade and oil flows already stressed by Hormuz issues. Further disruption to Red Sea shipping raises energy security concerns and insurance costs that can ripple into broader commodity and risk markets.
items.impact: Added shipping and oil supply risk premium
